title: Emergent ferromagnetism in the NiI$_2$-NbSe$_2$ van der Waals heterostructure
authors: Büşra Gamze Arslan, Mohammad Amini, Ziying Wang, Alessandro Orsini, Jose L. Lado, Adolfo O. Fumega, Robert Drost, Peter Liljeroth
abstract: Multiferroicity arising from non-collinear spin textures and strong spin-orbit interactions offers a route to magnetoelectric functionality in the monolayer limit. Although theory predicts that the properties of monolayer multiferroics can be tuned by strain, gating, or proximity effects, experimental demonstrations of such control remain scarce. Here we show that the magnetic ground state of monolayer NiI$_2$, a prototypical two-dimensional multiferroic, is altered by proximity to a superconducting NbSe$_2$ substrate. Using low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), we show that the metallic substrate renormalizes the exchange interactions within NiI$_2$ and drives it into a ferromagnetic ground state. This can be visualized by probing the Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) states within the superconducting gap of the NbSe$_2$ substrate. Our results establish YSR states as an in situ probe of two-dimensional magnetism and demonstrate substrate engineering as a means of controlling magnetic order in atomically thin materials.
summary: This work demonstrates that coupling the multiferroic $	ext{NiI}_2$ monolayer to a superconducting $	ext{NbSe}_2$ substrate drives a fundamental change in its magnetic state, forcing it from a helimagnetic to a ferromagnetic configuration. This control is experimentally verified by observing characteristic Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states using low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate experimental control over magnetic order, specifically driving a transition from a helimagnetic to a ferromagnetic state in monolayer $	ext{NiI}_2$ using proximity effects from a superconducting substrate.
main_result: The coupling of $	ext{NiI}_2$ to the $	ext{NbSe}_2$ substrate renormalizes exchange interactions, inducing a robust ferromagnetic ground state confirmed by spectroscopic signatures.
method: The research combines low-temperature Scanning Tunneling Microscopy/Spectroscopy ($	ext{STM}/	ext{STS}$) with theoretical modeling using Bogoliubov-de-Gennes Hamiltonians to predict and interpret the electronic states.
model_or_system: The system is a van der Waals heterostructure of monolayer $	ext{NiI}_2$ (a multiferroic) placed on a superconducting $	ext{NbSe}_2$ substrate. The physics involves coupling magnetic exchange interactions ($H_J$) to the intrinsic $s$-wave superconductivity ($H_{SC}$).
key_observables: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov ($	ext{YSR}$) states within the superconducting gap, reduction of coherence peaks in $	ext{STS}$ spectra, and spatial patterns of Local Density of States ($	ext{LDOS}$).
important_parameters: Low temperature (e.g., $350 	ext{ mK}$), proximity coupling strength, and the transition between helimagnetic and ferromagnetic magnetic order.
main_assumptions: The observed $	ext{YSR}$ states are directly attributable to the substrate-induced renormalization of the magnetic ground state in $	ext{NiI}_2$.
figures_summary: Figures show atomic structure, $	ext{STS}$ spectra comparing bare and coupled systems (showing gap filling/$	ext{YSR}$ bands), and theoretical predictions for $	ext{LDOS}$ patterns corresponding to different magnetic states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system ($	ext{NiI}_2/	ext{NbSe}_2$), uses theory ($	ext{DFT}/	ext{BdG}$) to predict the transition from spin spiral to ferromagnetic state, and validates this prediction using low-temperature $	ext{STS}$ measurements focusing on $	ext{YSR}$ states.
why_interesting: The ability to use superconducting proximity effects (a quantum phenomenon) to tune magnetic ordering in 2D materials provides a powerful platform for realizing controllable quantum magnets relevant to spintronics and topological physics.
